Allocation, lifetime, locking and error propagation for paged input output and commit objects.
Retry and completion transitions among header dispositions and their interaction with direct and layout paths.

findings.text: NFS 4.2 allocation and copy exchanges share a sequencing envelope around operation state. An allocation request pairs one file handle with open state plus a byte range plus a desired attribute mask, and its reply pairs status with refreshed attributes plus server identity. A copy request pairs source handle and position with destination handle and position plus length plus a synchronous hint plus a source server descriptor, and its reply pairs a write outcome of state plus count plus verifier with flags for consecutiveness and synchronicity plus a commit outcome.

Offload status, copy notification and seek exchanges each carry sequencing state alongside progress data. Status polling supplies a source handle with open state and returns transferred length plus a completion counter plus a finished indicator. Notification supplies a source handle with open state plus a destination server descriptor and returns lease duration plus new open state plus source server descriptor. Seek supplies a handle with open state plus start offset plus a selector for desired extent kind and returns status plus an end indicator plus the located offset.

Extended attribute exchanges bundle sequencing state with target handle and name plus paging for values. Setting adds an attribute mask plus flags plus length plus pages for content and returns change details plus fresh attributes plus server identity. Reading supplies name plus length plus pages and returns resulting length. Listing supplies a count plus cookie plus pages and returns a scratch holder plus buffer plus length plus next cookie plus end and copied indicators. Removal supplies a mask plus name and returns change details plus attributes plus server identity.
Inline page vector capacity is 8 entries, defining how many page pointers can be held without separate allocation.

Small page collection groups an external pointer with a maximum count plus an embedded store sized by the inline capacity, allowing use of the embedded store for small cases and larger storage otherwise.

Input output header dispositions form an ordered set of 8 values beginning at 0 for error and continuing through end, redo, status, two resend paths, unstable writes and direct mode, all sharing a common name prefix.

Header processing uses disposition values to steer retry and completion, distinguishing terminal error and end conditions from redo and status checks and from resubmission through either layout or metadata paths, while separately flagging unstable write handling and direct mode.

Parallel input output header aggregates file context, credential, page list, current request, write verifier, access mode, layout segment, start offset, server operations and several callbacks for release, completion and scheduling, plus completion tracking, direct request linkage and optional cache state. It also tracks retry count, layout and general errors, good byte boundary and flags, embeds task state plus attributes plus argument and result plus timestamp plus done callback plus stripe offset, and binds inline page storage with data server identity plus commit and mirror indexes. A companion commit summary counts outstanding remote calls and total commits plus a queue of pending work.

Commit handling separates completion policy, per inode context and per operation data. Completion policy pairs a finish action with a write rescheduling action. Per inode context links the inode with metadata and data server commit state plus optional direct request plus completion policy. Per operation data links task, inode, credential, attributes, verifier, coalesced and queued page lists, direct request, argument and result, open context, layout segment, data server identity and index, low water mark, server operations, completion policy, done callback and flags. Unlink data pairs remove arguments and result with dentry, credential, directory attributes and timeout. Rename data pairs rename arguments and result with task, credential, old and new directories plus dentries plus attributes, completion callback, timeout and cancellation flag.

Versioned client operations vector centralizes filesystem behavior for one protocol version, including root and mount handling, server lifecycle and trunk discovery, namespace lookup and mutation, link and symbolic link handling, directory iteration and entry decoding, attribute access and mutation, size and capability queries, paged read and write plus commit with setup prepare and completion stages, byte range locking with bounds checking, access cache management, open context lifecycle, delegation checks and return, and swap enablement. Operation tables for dentries, directories, files and lock management are referenced through the same vector.

Fixed size opaque handling encodes and decodes exact byte ranges with alignment awareness. Encoding reserves room, copies content and reports aligned footprint, warning once on failure in the thin wrapper. Decoding obtains a contiguous window, copies out and advances past padding, mapping short input to a bad message signal at stream level and to an input output failure in the thin wrapper.
Four byte unit conversion rounds any byte length upward to a count of four byte quantities, and stream alignment rounds any size upward to a multiple of the cross platform unit.
Access control limits allow up to 1024 entries overall and 5 entries inline, with word, page and byte budgets derived from those counts plus page size and fixed headers.
Access control size estimation starts from a fixed header allowance and adds per entry allowances for access and default lists, applying minimum entry counts when lists are absent or small.

Local input output identity groups a universal identifier with a probe counter, a cache aligned guard, membership linkage, a pointer to an external list guard, a reference counted network context held for safe release, an authentication domain and a list of locally opened files retained for shutdown or export change.

Identity guarding keeps a private spin guard on its own cache line for local state, delegates membership protection to an external list guard supplied by the network context, and holds the network context under read copy update so release remains safe against module unload.

Local server operations vector offers predicates to acquire and release network references, to open a file by handle under credentials and mode while returning both a direct file and a reference counted local handle, to release that handle while reporting whether network release is still required, to obtain the underlying file object, and to query direct input output alignment, with the whole vector aligned to avoid cache contention.

Network and file release helpers always execute the underlying release under read side protection and only release the network when the file release reports one, requiring callers to either guarantee a valid local handle or block shutdown completion while the identifier remains referenced.
Close, initialization and per client disable helpers are inert placeholders that perform no action and report no status, preserving call sites when the feature is unavailable.

Topology performance description pairs bandwidth and latency for reads and writes, classifies locality as near, processor associated or upper bound, and describes caches through indexing style, write policy, total size, line size, level and address mode drawn from small fixed enumerations.
Compute node object embeds a generic device plus a list of access descriptors, optionally extended with cache attribute list and cache device when heterogeneous memory reporting is enabled.

First and last memory lifecycle notifications use 6 distinct single bit flags for adding, added, cancelled adding, removing, removed and cancelled removing, and the notification payload carries the numeric node identifier.

Cache, performance, memory block, notifier and device helpers in this configuration accept their normal arguments and return success without effect, covering cache addition, performance set and update, hotplug and bulk memory registration, notifier registration and unregistration plus event delivery, and device initialization with node and processor association plus memory block removal.

Hotplug registration binds a callback with a priority into a statically held notifier block and registers it, with an inline variant that reports success directly, while device conversion recovers the enclosing node object from its embedded device member.

Speculation hardening provides an empty barrier plus a bounds mask helper that hides the index from optimization and yields an all ones mask inside bounds and zero outside using arithmetic and shift, plus a clamping macro that applies that mask with compile time width checks on index and size.

Short or missing reservation during fixed opaque transfer must not be treated as success, since encode signals message size exhaustion and decode signals malformed input, with thin wrappers converting those into a one time warning or a generic input output failure.
Each public header defines a single inclusion guard macro that makes repeated inclusion idempotent for access control, local input output, topology, speculation and namespace common types.
